title: Private audit-forwarder: customer-managed storage & secure forwarding for on-prem/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a production-grade audit log forwarding subsystem for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that supports customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Azure & S3-compatible), on‑prem syslog/Elasticsearch/Kafka endpoints, and secure push/pull modes. Key goals: 1) ensure tamper-evident delivery and strong encryption (TLS mTLS + optional customer KMS/HSM envelope), 2) integrate with RBAC v2 so only authorized admins can configure/read forwarding targets, 3) provide configurable batching, backpressure, and disk-spooling for offline durability, 4) support retention & lifecycle policies that respect customer-managed storage, and 5) include observability and test harness for customer acceptance tests.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Aisha: Kickoff notes: stakeholder list includes Security, Compliance, Private Delivery, Ops. Primary use-cases: audit export for long-term retention in customer-owned buckets, push to on-prem SIEMs, and cross-account delivery for SOC2 evidence. Created confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Audit+Forwarding+Spec

2026-02-18 - Marco: Architecture proposal v1 posted in the spec. Two deployment models: (A) in-cluster forwarder sidecar that signs and pushes logs to customer endpoints; (B) centralized relay in customer VPC with pull connectors. Preference leaning to sidecar for per-node isolation and to keep delivery within customer network. Trade-off: sidecar increases per-node resource usage vs relay centralization single point of failure.

2026-02-24 - Security review (initial): requested mTLS for all endpoints, enforce TLS1.3, require server cert validation, and flag requirement for KMS integration for customer-managed key encryption. Also requested HMAC signature on batches for tamper-evidence. Action: add envelope encryption and signature header metadata for later verification.

2026-03-02 - Marco: Prototype done for S3-compatible target (minio local) using signed v4 and optional SSE-C headers. Disk spooling uses LZ4 compressed files encrypted with node-local key; node-local key protected using platform KMS integration when present. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/relay/pull/592

2026-03-04 - Design feedback (Liam Chen): audit record schema must include immutable event id, sequence number, and signing metadata. Also recommended JSON-LD context so customers can map events to their SIEMs. Will update schema in spec.

2026-03-08 - Marco: Implemented RBAC v2 checks: only roles with audit.forwarder.manage or admin.* can create forwarder configs. Forwarder config objects are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) on the control plane; in Private mode these configs are surfaced to the local forwarder via the private control channel with mutual auth. Unit tests added. See test matrix: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1abcAuditMatrix

2026-03-11 - QA: Reported intermittent 413 errors when pushing large batched files to customer endpoints (Azure blob). Created follow-up: implement chunked uploads + automatic retry with exponential backoff and jitter. Added label 'retry-policy'.

2026-03-12 - PM (Nora Patel): Updated acceptance criteria: support S3 (AWS + compat), GCS, Azure Blob, syslog (tcp/tls), Elasticsearch/Kafka, on-prem HTTP collectors. Provide two delivery guarantees: 'at-least-once' (default) and 'exactly-once-ish' with de-duplication tokens for customers that enable sequencing. Beta customers identified: AcmeHealth (HIPAA) and FinTrade (EU data residency).
